deck_zh: 一个人想走，一个人被赶走，还有一些孩子一直没有被接住。国籍的难题，不只在护照上。
deck_en: An engineer tries to leave. A critic is pushed out. Children wait for a country to recognize them. Citizenship is about more than a passport.
body_zh: 那位工程师原本每天往返于两个国家之间。她三十四岁，住在高岭邦，在北邻目的民族联盟的一家水电公司上班。后来，对方的一个区政府聘她任公职，条件是取得目的民族联盟的国籍，并在六个月内放弃目的联合城邦的国籍。她去办手续，申请却被退了回来。
本系列的国家与人物都是虚构的。可她遇到的那种局促并不难理解：一边说，你得先放下原来的身份；另一边说，现在不许你放。目的联合城邦发了紧急令，战时暂停受理十九岁至四十五岁者的离籍申请。柜台没有审她还欠不欠税，也没有审别的条件。只要年龄落在那一段，事情就到这里。
六个月过去，新国籍的批准失效。次年春天，她拿着工作许可搬了过去，仍是原国公民。同一个春天，征召令寄到她已经不住的地址。她没有应征，被立案调查。又过了一年多，战时状态终止，她重新申请，缴税、交费，终于离籍。案子仍挂着，没有起诉。
说她最后还是走成了，当然没错。可这句话太省事了。它略过了失效的批准，也略过了那些年里，她的下一步为什么始终握在别人手中。
## 走得出去，才不只是被留下
离开一座城市，还能搬到同一国家的另一座城市。离开一个国家，却没有更高一层负责接住你。你只能去另一个国家，还得等它接纳。因此，国籍不是可以随意撕掉的一张纸；也正因此，它尤其不能成为把人拴住的绳子。
这里提出的是一条规范主张，不是对各国现行法律的介绍：退出不该是国家给人的恩典。国家可以登记，可以要求清结已经欠下的税，已经提起的诉讼也不会因为一个人离境就消失。但国家不能靠关住人来维持自身。它所保护的生活，不能一到需要保护时，反而变成它可以扣留的资源。防守的战争也不例外。
工程师面前还有一笔钱。离籍清算税把她没有卖掉的资产视同出售，对增值收取百分之十八；另有相当于三个月平均工资的离籍费。按她的资产，清算税大约要拿走四分之一积蓄。它们不同于早已欠下的税：这笔代价，是因为她要走才出现的。定价的一方应当说明，它究竟在清什么账，为什么是这个数。付不起的人，也得有一条不由收费一方把住的申诉路，而不能只听见一句，标准对所有人都一样。
暂缓离籍的紧急令更直接。她的身体可以跨境，身份却仍把她留在征召之内。若人已离境，还可以因为拒不应征而受到新追诉，离开就只剩两种后果：回来服役，或者不敢回来。在本文的主张里，这仍是用另一种办法限制离开，不因征召令早一天或晚一天送达而改变。离境前已经起诉的案件可以继续审，但不以此扣人、加重处罚或挂住离籍。
已经应征、正在服役的人擅自离开岗位，是另一件事：那里有具体岗位的责任，应由司法程序处理，不能和未进入岗位的人混成一类；离境本身也不另加一项罪。对不愿持武器的人，还应有随时提出、进入独立审查的路。后一篇会讲到它。这里不是把一切责任一笔勾销，而是不许把离开本身写成一笔还不完的债。
## 不让走，也不能随手赶走
同一国家里，另一位女性遇到了相反的事。她生在南湾邦，住在北邻，为本国刊物写专栏。她反对修宪，反对军队越河，发起停战请愿，得到四十一万人联署。后来，成员登记署署长以危害国家存续为由，撤销了她的国籍。她没有别的国籍，护照当天作废。
她可以起诉，期限三十天。但法院要求本人去河口城递交，入境部门又说，非本国公民入境须经审查。五个月没有答复。律师替她递交，法院退回：程序不符。每一个窗口似乎都有自己的根据，窗口合在一起，却让她无处发问。直到次年秋天，法院承认代交有效，案件才进入审理。
国籍连着选票，也连着许多能够主张权利的位置。行政机关因为一个人质疑自己，就拿走她作为问者的资格，这已经不只是如何惩罚某种言论了，而是在决定：以后还有没有你这个人来问。把人推到门外，不会让问题消失；她仍被撤籍的后果追着走，国家仍在追她的言论，彼此的关系一点也没有干净地结束。
因此，本文不赋予任何行政机关剥夺国籍的权力。对一个人的行为，可以依法起诉，由法院裁判；但因出生取得的国籍，不能作为惩罚被收回，也不因她还有另一国护照就可以收回。经申请取得的国籍有一处区别：如果取得时存在欺诈，法院可以审查那次取得是否成立。审的是当时的欺诈，不是后来令人不快的言行；不能把撤籍换个名称，叫作当初就不该让你进来。
另一些人的问题，不是资格被收走，而是始终没有拿到。柳渡镇以北的接收中心住着六千三百人，出门要领许可，早六点到晚八点有效。有些人坐早班车去苹果城做零工，再赶回来。这里出生的三百一十个孩子，出生证上国籍一栏写着：未定。
父母的原国不为他们登记；这里的法律又要求父母合法居留满五年，暂留的年月不算。一位母亲到第十一年才获得庇护，于是孩子最早得等到第十六年才有资格申请。孩子已经在这里生活，时间却仿佛还没有开始。
我们很容易把这种人叫作身份有问题的人。可需要解释的，首先是分类与生活为什么对不上。国家安排他们住在哪里、几点能出门、喝谁供的水、孩子去哪里上课，却又说，他们尚未取得可以被接住的身份。不能一面深入组织一个人的生活，一面把他长期放在临时二字里。

这里要分清今天与将来。今天，他们就应该能投诉、获得答复与救济，不等入籍。将来，对生在这里、在这里生活又无国可归的孩子，应有一条真实可走、有期限的入籍道路；期限不能等到拒收的一方愿意让它开始时才开始。已经实际接收、因别国剥夺国籍而无处可归的成年人，也需要这样的路，条件按本国实际组织其生活的程度说明。即便法院认定一次申请取得国籍存在欺诈，由此无籍的人也不能被永远悬空：欺诈可计入新路径的条件，不把路径改成没有终点的等待。
这些主张并不等于人人自动取得国籍。一个境外的人受到本国某项措施影响，有权追问那项措施，也不因此自动得到入籍的资格。受到什么影响，与应当取得什么身份，要分别回答。但没有身份，不能成为连第一声求助都不必听见的理由。
## 国界画到哪里，问题就停在哪里吗
西关口岸曾接到十四名越境投到的邻国士兵。两国协议要求七十二小时内交还，每人谈话大约十分钟。三人说不愿回去，一人说回去要坐牢。主任的批注只有一句：依议定书办理。后来有刊物说，其中两人被判了十五年；目的联合城邦没有核实。我们不能把未经核实的报道写成已经确定的后果。
可是，在那七十二小时里，有没有一个独立于交还决定的地方，能够接到他们的不愿意？这已经可以问。两国订过约，不等于站在柜台前的人失去了自己的问题。申诉若要等交还之后才能开始，对这十四个人就可能从来没有开始过。
后来，口岸限流，桥西排起上万人的长队，等六至九天，有妇女在桥上生产，也有老人在寒夜里死亡。桥西属于邻国，那里没有接待设施，是邻国应答的事；但本国一天放行多少、放行多快，仍是本国要答的事。两边不能互相替对方销账。一个人站在国界另一侧，不会让这边落到他身上的决定突然变成没有对象。对他的拘留、拒入、遣返，都要有他够得着、用了不遭报复的独立审查；这不等于本国获得了治理对岸的权限，也不等于他自动成为公民。
离开有时还会是一整个地区的事。南湾邦公投，投票率百分之六十三，赞成退出者占百分之五十二点四。港口两个区多数赞成，北部三个区多数反对。宪章没有写退出，中央执政院据此宣布公投无效，拒绝谈判。可当初立宪时，可以退出与不得退出两个提案都没有通过。沉默并不是一张偷偷留给中央的永久否决票。
一次公投也不能把所有事情处置干净：不愿离开的人，共用的港口、海关与基地，留下国家里与他们相连的人，都不会因为多数已定而消失。需要的是一条能启动、能形成决定、能处理僵局的公共程序。启动不靠中央先同意；程序也不把一方的宣布当成所有共同事项的终点。门槛可以高，但得有走通的现实可能；需要谈判，也不等于每一个相关方都有权永远不合作。未结的账，不得把退出无限期拖住。
这篇没有替南湾邦决定该走还是该留。它只是坚持，留下与离开都不能由最有力量的一方替所有人说完。即使程序走完，仍要记得它没有接住谁、切开了哪些原本相连的生活。就像那位工程师终于换了国籍，不能倒过来说，既然最后办成了，之前那些年便从未有人欠过她一个回答。
body_en: For years, the engineer had crossed the border on her way to work. She was thirty-four, lived in the Highland State, and worked for a hydropower company in the northern neighbor, the Nation Union of Telos. Then a district government there offered her a public-service job. She could have it if she became a citizen—and relinquished her citizenship of the United City-States of Ends within six months.

These countries and their inhabitants are fictional. The predicament is easier to recognize: one state says you must give up your old status; the other says you may not. A wartime emergency order had suspended renunciation applications from everyone aged nineteen to forty-five. The registry returned her application without considering the remaining conditions.

The six months elapsed. Her citizenship approval expired. The following spring she moved north on a work permit, still a UCSE citizen. A call-up order went to the address she had left. She did not report, and prosecutors opened an investigation. Not until the state of war ended, more than a year later, could she apply again, pay the charges, and renounce. The investigation remained open; no charges had been brought.
She got out eventually. That is true, but too convenient. It leaves out the opportunity that expired, and the years in which someone else held the next step of her life.
## A door you can actually use

Leave a city and you can move to another city in the same country. Leave a state and no higher authority is waiting to receive you. Another state must agree to take you in. Citizenship is not a piece of paper one can casually tear up. Precisely for that reason, it must not become a leash.

The argument here is normative, not a description of existing citizenship law. A state may register departure and settle taxes already owed. Existing prosecutions need not vanish. What it may not do is preserve itself by sealing people in. Even a defensive war does not turn those it protects into a reserve of human material it may retain by force.

Money presented a separate obstacle. Renunciation would trigger a tax treating the engineer's unsold assets as though she had sold them, charging eighteen percent on the gains—roughly a quarter of her savings. There was also a fee of three average monthly wages. These were not simply old debts: leaving itself generated the bill. The state must explain what it is settling and why that price is justified. Someone unable to pay needs an independent route to challenge the obstacle, not an assurance that everyone faces the same fee.

The emergency order dispensed with even that discussion. Her body could cross the border, but her retained citizenship kept her within reach of conscription. A new prosecution for refusing a call-up after she had left would do the same work: return to serve, or risk never returning. On this argument, the date on which the notice arrived does not change the function. Proceedings already brought before departure can continue, but cannot be used to detain her, block departure or renunciation, or increase punishment because she left.

Leaving a post after entering military service is different. There is then a particular role and its responsibilities, to be addressed through courts rather than a commander's unchecked decision. Crossing the border adds no separate offense. A serving person must also have an available route to claim conscientious objection to bearing arms. Keeping these distinctions is not abolishing responsibility. It is refusing to turn departure itself into an unpayable debt.
## Who gets to belong?

A commentator faced the opposite treatment. Born in South Bay State and living in the northern neighbor, she wrote for UCSE publications, opposed the constitutional amendment and the army's river crossing, and organized a peace petition signed by 410,000 people. The head of the membership registry revoked her citizenship for threatening the country's survival. She held no other citizenship. Her passport became invalid that day.

She had thirty days to sue, but had to file in person in Rivermouth City. The entry office said that, as a noncitizen, she needed clearance. Five months passed without an answer. A lawyer's filing was rejected. Each office followed its own rule; together, the offices made a challenge impossible. Only the following autumn did the court accept filing through a representative.

Citizenship carries a vote and many other practical means of making a claim. When an administration removes a critic's citizenship, it is not merely responding to something she said. It is removing her standing to ask who should hold office. An institution under question must not be able to eliminate its questioner.

The proposal is therefore stronger than a ban on arbitrary administrative decisions. No administrative office may strip citizenship. Conduct can be prosecuted and judged; citizenship acquired by birth cannot be taken back as punishment, even if another passport is available. Citizenship obtained by application has a narrow distinction: a court can examine fraud in the acquisition itself. That does not authorize punishment for later speech under the fiction that the person should never have been admitted.

Others have never received the status in the first place. At a reception center north of Willow Ferry, 6,300 people live on temporary permits. They need passes to leave, valid between six in the morning and eight at night. Some commute to casual jobs in Apple City. For 310 children born at the center, the citizenship field on the birth certificate reads 'undetermined.'

Their parents' former country refuses registration. UCSE law offers an application after five years of a parent's lawful residence, but temporary stays do not count. One mother obtained asylum in Year 11; her child could not apply until Year 16. The child was already living here. Official time had not begun.

We call these people cases with a status problem. Yet the first explanation is owed by the categories that fail to accommodate them. The state decides where they live, when they can go out, who supplies their water, and how their children are taught. It cannot organize almost an entire life while leaving that life indefinitely 'temporary.'

Two obligations have different clocks. Access to complaints, answers, and remedies is due now, without waiting for citizenship. For stateless children born and living here, there must also be a real, time-bounded path to membership. The authority withholding recognition cannot indefinitely withhold the date on which the clock starts. Stateless adults actually received into the country need such a path too, with conditions explained by how extensively the country organizes their lives. Even when a court finds fraud in a citizenship application, a resulting stateless person cannot be left permanently suspended: the fraud may inform conditions on a new path, but cannot remove its endpoint.

None of this makes citizenship automatic. Nor does someone abroad acquire a path to citizenship merely because a UCSE measure affects them. Access to challenge that measure and entitlement to membership are different questions. Lacking membership, however, cannot mean having no claim to be heard at all.
## The people at the border

Fourteen soldiers from the Democratic Republic of Purposes crossed into UCSE territory and gave themselves up at West Pass. A bilateral agreement required return within seventy-two hours. Interviews lasted about ten minutes each. Three said they would not go back; one said he would be imprisoned. The crossing director's note read: handled under the protocol. A later report alleged that two received fifteen-year sentences. UCSE had not verified it, and we cannot treat the allegation as an established outcome.

We can already ask whether, within those seventy-two hours, they could reach anyone independent of the office deciding their return. A treaty between countries does not dispose of the people standing at the counter. A challenge available only after removal might never have been available to them at all.

Later, daily entry limits left thousands queuing on the bridge's western end for six to nine days. A woman gave birth there; two elderly people died on cold nights. The western end belonged to the other country. Its failure to provide reception facilities was its responsibility. UCSE's admission rate remained UCSE's responsibility. Neither account canceled the other. Decisions can reach people across a border, even where the deciding state has no territorial authority. Those people need an independent, reachable, nonretaliatory way to challenge refusal, return, or detention. That does not confer citizenship, or give UCSE a right to govern the other bank.

Sometimes it is a region that wants to leave. South Bay's referendum drew 63 percent turnout, with 52.4 percent voting for independence. Two port districts strongly favored departure; three northern districts strongly opposed it. The national executive called the vote legally ineffective because the Charter said nothing about secession. But the founding convention had rejected both an express right to leave and an express prohibition. Silence was not a permanent veto secretly reserved for the center.

One regional majority cannot settle everything either: dissenting residents, shared ports, customs arrangements, naval facilities, and people elsewhere remain involved. A workable public procedure must allow initiation without the national executive's permission, produce decisions, and resolve deadlock. Its thresholds may be demanding, but realistically attainable. Joint procedure cannot mean every interested party gets to obstruct forever, or that unresolved assets postpone departure indefinitely.

This essay does not decide whether South Bay should leave. It insists that neither staying nor leaving may be spoken for entirely by the strongest party. Even a completed procedure must acknowledge the claims it missed and the lives its new boundary divided. The engineer eventually obtained a different passport. That does not mean nobody owed her an answer during the years before.
